subject.title: fix(memory-wiki): bound apply body file reads

question: Should `wiki apply synthesis --body-file` adopt 1 MiB as its supported maximum for existing users, or should the limit be derived from an already-established memory-wiki contract?
rationale: The code is technically bounded, but choosing a new hard rejection limit changes compatibility for existing CLI automation and cannot be resolved safely from the PR’s current evidence alone.

options.title: Define and prove the supported limit
options.body: Before merge, tie the cap to an existing contract or document the intended 1 MiB limit and add upgrade-facing proof for both accepted and rejected inputs.

options.title: Accept the new 1 MiB contract
options.body: Merge with explicit owner acceptance that larger existing body files are intentionally unsupported going forward.

recommendation.title: Define and prove the supported limit
recommendation.body: Before merge, tie the cap to an existing contract or document the intended 1 MiB limit and add upgrade-facing proof for both accepted and rejected inputs.

likelyOwner.reason: The available evidence identifies this contributor as the author of the proposed boundary; merged-area ownership was not established in the available history evidence.
